text:
maya: Heads-up — seeing a perf regression on A100 after the kernel-picker tweak. P95 +12%, throughput -8% for seq_len=512 batches. nvprof shows a big increase in register spills for the selected kernel. Link to profile: https://perf.redwood/job/2012/profile/321

liam: Can you paste the kernel-picker decision / config used for that run? My hunch is tile size got bumped and caused reg pressure.

maya: Here is the selector output for that run:
```
kernel_choice: {
  tile_size: 128,
  warp_specialization: true,
  smem_per_warp_kb: 6,
  regs_per_thread: 64,
  estimated_occupancy: 0.60,
  fallback: null
}
```

zara: That explains it. A100's register file behavior + our SMEM layout means tile=128 pushes register pressure over the spill threshold for some layers. H100 would be more forgiving but A100 will spill and kill p95.

ben: Proposal: add a quick reg-spill check into the autotuner. Microbenchmark per-arch that sweeps tile sizes and measures "reg_spill_rate" (from nvprof counters). Pick largest tile where spill_rate < 1%.

infra-bot: perf-runner: started job perf/5678 (canary) for maya — https://perf.redwood/job/5678

liam: I ran a quick canary: forcing tile_size=64 for seq_len in [256,1024] reduced p95 by ~10% on A100, throughput stayed flat. Pushed branch selector/tilesize-a100-fix with conditional rule: if device.family==a100 and regs_per_thread>48 -> prefer tile_size=64.

maya: Nice. I'll run KV cache correctness and eviction-impact tests — the change shouldn't affect prefix caching but want to confirm LRU churn for mixed batch sizes.

zara: :thumbsup: Also add a fallback that allows tile=128 if short-batch latency regresses >5% (we saw one edge case where smaller tiles blow up for tiny batches).

ben: Filed a small spec for autotuner: add reg_spill_rate metric, arch thresholds, and a synthetic microbenchmark harness. I'll open a PR with tests.

maya: Created bug INF-842 with profile artifacts and test results. CC @eng-runtime. We'll monitor canary for 24h and then roll to prod if stable.
